nuggets.title: Fraud scoring breaches checkout latency SLO

scenario.symptoms: Checkout p99 rose from 180 ms to 950 ms after enabling a new graph feature. The fraud service blocks the payment API synchronously on every request.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Feature lookup hits a remote graph service with p95 400 ms. There is no timeout fallback or async shadow scoring path.

incident.headline: Synchronous graph feature fetch dominates checkout latency

agenda.goal: Keep fraud decisions within checkout latency budget.
agenda.opener: Checkout slowed after fraud graph features—how do you meet the latency SLO without turning fraud off?

evidence.strong: Precomputed features in low-latency store, strict timeouts, degrade to rules/light model, async enrichment for review queue.
evidence.adequate: Caches graph calls but still blocks on cache miss without fallback.
evidence.weak: Adds more graph servers only, still synchronous.

misconceptions.pattern: Assuming horizontal scale fixes tail latency on the critical path.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens on a cache miss during peak?

probes: Which features must be synchronous vs review-queue?
What default decision applies when scoring times out?
hints: Separate real-time path from batch graph analytics.
agenda.referenceFix: Serve hot features from Redis/feature store, cap graph RPC at tens of ms with fallback score, and route heavy features to async human review rather than blocking authorize.

nuggets.title: Hot merchant key melts feature store

scenario.symptoms: A flash sale on one merchant drove fraud feature Redis CPU to 100%. Latency correlated with a single feature key read millions of times per minute.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Features are keyed only by merchant id without local caching on scoring nodes. All fraud workers hammer the same Redis shard.

incident.headline: Single merchant feature key becomes a hot spot in Redis

agenda.goal: Serve high-QPS features without hot-key collapse.
agenda.opener: One merchant sale saturated Redis on a single key—how would you fix feature serving?

evidence.strong: Local in-process cache with short TTL, read replicas, key splitting, proactive refresh, and monitoring hot keys.
evidence.adequate: Bigger Redis instance without local cache.

probes: How stale can a locally cached merchant feature be for fraud?
When do you shard a hot key?
hints: Same patterns as viral URL short codes.
agenda.referenceFix: Add per-node LRU for top merchant features, use Redis read replicas, detect hot keys automatically, and pre-warm features before known sales.

scenario.symptoms: When the ML scoring cluster crashed for 12 minutes, checkout returned HTTP 503 for every card payment. No rule-based fallback path existed.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Architecture treats model score as mandatory gate with fail-closed policy and no degraded mode.

incident.headline: Hard dependency on ML scorer stops payments during model outage

agenda.goal: Keep payments flowing with safe degradation when ML is unavailable.
agenda.opener: Model cluster down and checkout hard-stopped—what fallback strategy balances risk and availability?

evidence.strong: Tiered fallback to rules/light model, circuit breaker, tightened limits during degrade, and post-hoc review queue.
evidence.adequate: Fail open to approve all—high fraud risk.
evidence.weak: Fail closed 503 with no alternate path.

misconceptions.pattern: Automatically approving all transactions when ML is down.
misconceptions.challenge: What fraud exposure does unlimited approve create in 12 minutes?

probes: Which signals can rules evaluate without the full model?
How do you communicate degraded mode to risk ops?
agenda.referenceFix: Circuit-break to rules engine with lower amount thresholds, velocity limits, and manual review backlog; restore ML when healthy and re-score async.
